errors.description: The conversion of a teacher-sampled negative log-likelihood into teacher/model KL divergences is mathematically invalid as written.
errors.evidence: Equation (6) uses log(P_teacher(a_j | s, a_<j) / log P_pi(a_j | s, a_<j)). For positive teacher probability and 0 < P_pi < 1, the ratio is negative and its real logarithm is undefined. Even replacing the denominator with P_pi would not make a single observed-token log ratio equal to KL, which requires an expectation over the teacher token distribution.

errors.location: Section 3 theoretical analysis, Equations (9)-(11), generalized EM interpretation
errors.description: The claimed generalized-EM interpretation and formal superiority are not established by the displayed updates.
errors.evidence: Equation (9) optimizes E_{a~pi}[r_pi(s,a)], whereas Equation (10) freezes the sampling distribution at pi_t. No EM lower bound or ascent inequality connects this surrogate to Equation (9). With policy-dependent rewards, optimizing the frozen expectation need not improve the original expectation; setting pi_{t+2} = pi_{t+1} supplies no such guarantee.

errors.location: Section 4.1, Decoding Strategy; Section 4.2, state-of-the-art comparison and Table 1 caption
errors.description: Selecting decoding settings using the evaluation scores can inflate reported performance and undermine the claimed superiority over literature baselines.
errors.evidence: The model is tested at temperatures {0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8}, and "For each test metric (pass@1, pass@5, and pass@10), the best result is chosen." Selecting the maximum on the test benchmark introduces selection optimism and can use different policies for different metrics. Table 1 imports baseline results from other papers without establishing equivalent selection, while Section 4.2 attributes the score differences to the training method.
